department: Department of Materials Science and Engineering

deadline.value: The admissions page mentions a January application deadline for tests but gives no PhD deadline date; confirm with the department.
deadline.quote: we recommend taking your tests in October in order to meet the January application deadline.

fee_waiver.value: Highly qualified PhD applicants may petition for a fee waiver; endorsement by a faculty member is advised.
fee_waiver.quote: *Highly qualified Ph.D. students may petition for an application fee waiver at this link.

gre_general.value: GRE is not required but highly recommended by the department.
gre_general.quote: GRE Score (Not required, but highly recommended by department)

supervisor.value: Contacting professors is optional, but you must list preferred faculty on the application.
supervisor.quote: A. It is not required for consideration for admission or for support.

also.quote: You should indicate your preference for faculty advisors in your online application via Slate.

funding.value: Support is mostly research assistantships from individual professors; the department offers no scholarships and fellowships are very competitive.
funding.quote: Financial assistance, when offered, is usually in the form of a position as a research assistant.

also.quote: We don't offer scholarships for graduate students. The few fellowships available are extremely competitive.

entry_route.value: A bachelor's degree with at least a 3.0 GPA meets the graduate school minimum.
entry_route.quote: A bachelor's degree from a regionally-accredited college/university

gre_subject.value: The department does not mention a subject test.

notes: The same department also runs a Metallurgical Engineering PhD.
